summary: Tested v4 double-count-safe ledger (Members / Transfers / Reimbursements / Personal Contribution). Backend: 13/13 pytest cases passed in /app/backend/tests/test_ledger_v4.py, including the full acceptance scenario (clean slate → chandas → transfer → expense → personal expense → reimbursement) verifying dashboard.chanda.total_received stays 47000 (unchanged by transfer & reimbursement), Monu.reimbursement_due goes 15000 → 0, Shrikant.current_held = 5000, balance = 5000, and all invariants around split validation, overdraw and self-reimbursement. Frontend: BLOCKING SYNTAX ERROR in MemberDetail.jsx (missing MiniCard component + dangling code after export) was preventing the entire app from compiling — fixed. After fix, verified Dashboard shows advances-section + dashboard-reimburse-link + advance-row-Monu, Balance ₹12,000; Members page shows 3 tabs (Members/Transfers/Ledger) and reimburse-btn-Monu; MemberDetail shows reimb-due-banner + member-reimburse-btn; AddReimbursement TO dropdown lists ONLY 'Monu · Due: ₹15,000'; AddTransfer preview says 'This will not add to Total Chanda' and overdraw warning appears when amount > held; AddExpense submit disabled on split mismatch and shows exp-personal-note when personal>0; FAB/header add-sheet shows all 4 choices (add-chanda / add-transfer / add-reimbursement / add-expense).

issues: React console warning: <span> inside <option> (visual-editor injected span). Not user-visible but shows console error and can cause hydration mismatch in SSR contexts.

action_items: MemberDetail.jsx had a broken tail (dangling `const map`/`return` after component close, and MiniCard used but not defined). I renamed the leftover `Stat` function to `MiniCard` and added `amber` color. Please review — original intent may have had a separate Stat component elsewhere.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 947 lines — split into routers (chanda, collectors, expenses, transfers, reimbursements, members, dashboard, backup) before adding more.
compute_held and build_member_summaries fire N+1 queries per member (5 finds × N members). For 100+ members will be slow. Consider a single aggregation or in-memory pass over pre-fetched arrays.
PUT /api/expenses drops fields when caller sends null (same `v is not None` pattern as before) — can't unset vendor/note via PUT.

PUT /api/chanda: when status changes to Pending it forces received_amount=0 even if client explicitly sent a non-zero received_amount in same request (rule 'unless explicit' not honored for status=Pending path).
Reimbursement update endpoint does not enforce amount > 0 like create does.
MemberDetail.jsx had a broken tail leaving the app un-compilable — indicates missing lint/build gate before commit.
seed_data_creation: Tests call POST /api/restore replace-mode with empty arrays to wipe state, then create collectors Shrikant + Monu and full acceptance scenario data. UI verification left DB in state: Shrikant + Monu, chandas 27k, transfer 2k, personal-split expense 30k.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite /app/backend/tests/test_ledger_v4.py + existing test_expenses.py cover Chanda(promised/received) + Transfers + Expenses(split) + Reimbursements + Members/Ledger + Backup v4. Tests wipe DB via /api/restore replace-mode — do NOT run against a DB with production data. If MemberDetail.jsx is regenerated by main agent, ensure `MiniCard` (or the intended sub-component) is exported/defined; the previous check-in shipped a broken file that blocked the whole SPA.
rca of the issue: Frontend refused to load with 'return outside of function' SyntaxError at MemberDetail.jsx:214. Root cause: the file's tail contained dangling JSX + `const map` + `return` immediately after the exported component's closing `}`. Additionally the exported component referenced `<MiniCard>` while no such component existed in the module — the sub-component appears to have been half-renamed or partially deleted. Fix: reconstructed MiniCard function wrapper with the same color map (added amber). All routes then compiled and every acceptance UI selector became reachable.
